original_question: For a finite subscheme Gamma subseteq A^n, define the smoothability defect delta(Gamma) as the smallest possible difference deg(Gamma_prime) - deg(Gamma), where Gamma subseteq Gamma_prime and Gamma_prime is a finite smoothable scheme. What behavior can the function delta have, and can delta(Gamma) ever exceed deg(Gamma)?
target_in_paper: Problem XXXV in §2.9 (Smoothability): the smoothability defect of a finite subscheme of affine space.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly works with a finite subscheme Γ of affine space, defines the smoothability defect as the minimum extra degree needed to enlarge Γ to a finite smoothable scheme, and asks both parts that appear in the paper: the general behavior of the defect function and the concrete question whether the defect can exceed the degree of Γ.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k throughout (§1.3), so the ambient space should be A^n_k rather than an unspecified A^n.
The containing scheme Γ′ should be understood as a finite smoothable subscheme of the same ambient affine space A^n_k containing Γ scheme-theoretically, not merely as an abstract finite scheme.

Smoothability is meant in the Hilbert-scheme sense relevant to subschemes of affine space, i.e. belonging to the smoothable component of the Hilbert scheme of points (§2.1, used throughout the paper’s terminology).
The quantifier is over all finite subschemes Γ ⊂ A^n_k and all n; the paper does not restrict to a fixed dimension or fixed degree.

If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, it is helpful to state that the minimum is finite; the discussion immediately after Problem XXXV explains this and gives only an exponential general bound via monomial thickenings.
The neighboring asymptotic question about sequences of schemes is a separate Problem XXXVI and should not be merged into the Problem XXXV formulation.
refined_question:
Over an algebraically closed field k, let Γ ⊂ A^n_k be a finite subscheme. Define its smoothability defect by
δ(Γ) := min{deg(Γ′) - deg(Γ) : Γ ⊂ Γ′ ⊂ A^n_k and Γ′ is a finite smoothable k-scheme}.
What can be said about the function δ on finite subschemes of affine spaces? In particular, does there exist a finite subscheme Γ such that δ(Γ) > deg(Γ)?
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem XXXV in §2.9, and that problem is already almost exactly your formulation. I therefore kept the affine-space setting and the two-part question from Problem XXXV, while adding the paper’s standing convention that everything is over an algebraically closed field from §1.3 so that the question is fully stand-alone. I did not replace it by Problem XXXVI, because XXXVI is a separate asymptotic strengthening motivated by matrix multiplication rather than the nearest official formulation of your draft. The discussion immediately after Problem XXXV is also the relevant nearby context: it records that the defect is always finite, gives an exponential upper bound via monomial thickenings, and notes that in known examples the defect seems to be 1.
